mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-increase average (t-test p > 0.05) during the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 2,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with monthly PAYEMS increases (Pearson r < 0.2, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 102 suggests expanding economic demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in all months where INDPRO > 102 (direction consistency violated).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 233 over two consecutive months indicates a cooling demand environment, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day pre-cooling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market resilience that lowers policy rate expectations, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns higher.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with UNRATE < 4.0 regime (Spearman rho < 0.1, p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales (not available in proxy list) and manufacturing activity (indirectly proxy via HOUST > 1000) over a month suggests robust demand, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns when both proxies move together.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a significant positive interaction between HOUST and (hypothetical retail proxy, but only HOUST used here; thus this is a placeholder for interaction logic).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the monthly number of job openings (not directly available, but as a hypothetical: if PAYEMS declines by >10% from prior month while UNRATE remains flat, it indicates labor market cooling and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >10% from prior month and UNRATE is flat

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of falling short-term yields (indirectly inferred via FEDFUNDS < 4.0%), the S&P 60-day forward return tends to be positive due to lower discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day pre-low-rate average in any quarter (t-test p > 0.05).
